sections.name: TimelineController
sections.title: Timeline, pin and highlights routes
sections.what: The timeline route returns a page of events from the filters and writes a view audit. The pin route toggles an entry's pinned state. The highlights route returns the summary and writes a view audit.
sections.why: Likely reason: reading health data is audited, while pinning only changes the user's own ordering.
sections.watch_out: Filters are not checked, so an invalid page or limit goes straight into the service.

summary: Exposes the routes for reading the health timeline, pinning an entry, and getting timeline highlights.
purpose: Lets the app show the user's health history in order, with important entries pinned.
why: Likely reason: each read of health data is logged for privacy and audit reasons.
how: The timeline route reads filters from the query string, returns the page from the service, then writes a view audit entry. The pin route passes the event id and pin flag to the service. The summary route gets highlights and also writes an audit entry.
inputs: Signed-in user id, filter values from the query string, the event id, the pin flag from the body, and request details for the audit.
outputs: The timeline page with data and meta, the pin result, and the highlights.
risks: Filter values are not checked before use. The pin route writes no audit entry. The pin flag is not checked to be true or false. The audit is written after the data is read.
debug: For an empty timeline, check the user has timeline rows and the filters are not too narrow. For missing audit entries, check the route being used. For a pin that does nothing, check the event belongs to the user.
